content: Medications used to treat nocturia in adults are specifically aimed at addressing the underlying causes of excessive nighttime urination. These drugs may include desmopressin, which is a synthetic analog of vasopressin that reduces urine production during the night by concentrating the urine. Anticholinergic agents, such as oxybutynin or tolterodine, may be prescribed to manage overactive bladder symptoms by relaxing the detrusor muscle and reducing bladder contractions. Beta-3 adrenergic agonists, such as mirabegron, can also be utilized to improve bladder storage capacity by relaxing the bladder wall. In cases where nocturia is associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), alpha-blockers like tamsulosin or 5-alpha reductase inhibitors such as finasteride may be used to alleviate urinary obstruction. Diuretics, when timed appropriately earlier in the day, can help reduce fluid retention and minimize nighttime urine production. Additionally, non-pharmacological interventions, such as fluid restriction in the evening and addressing comorbid conditions like sleep apnea or diabetes, are often combined with these medications to optimize treatment outcomes.
